description: TerraVerdict audits claims about Earth trends (“the river is drying up”) with NASA data: what changes, where, by how much, is it significant? Verdicts: Supported, Contradicted or Inconclusive. Join us for real science and NASA data tools. Seeking: Earth science/hydrology, statistics/data, and storytelling/video people. No NASA experience needed. We work in Spanish and English.
summary:
Arequipa, Peru's second-largest city, lives on rain that falls on a 4,200 m Andean plateau. In just three years it suffered both faces of the same crisis: in 2023 its reservoirs dropped to 159 of 409 hm³ and 70 districts were declared in emergency; in 2025 turbidity hit 5,000 NTU and over 70% of the population lost drinking water. Ground data cannot explain why: the only GHCN rain gauge has no complete year since 2010.

TerraVerdict turns open NASA Earth-observation data into answers you can trust: WHAT is changing, WHY, with HOW MUCH confidence, and WHERE to act. It ingests NASA POWER, GPM IMERG (1998–2025), MODIS LST, GIBS and the Global Landslide Catalog with SHA-256 chain of custody; detects trends with a "Confidence Seal" (Sen/Mann-Kendall, ENSO removal, moving windows, independent data families); ranks which variables truly matter; and forecasts extreme rain and drought with 10 neural networks plus classical models, statistically validated against climatology (block bootstrap 90% CI + Diebold-Mariano).

Result: confirmed out-of-sample skill on all 7 published forecasts (e.g., 1-month drought SPI-3 skill 0.68), live for all 25 regions of Peru, in a bilingual web app with "Terra", an AI assistant that only answers with published evidence and numerically verifies every figure. Live with El Niño ONI +2.46 now. Science that refuses to overclaim.
details:
THE PROBLEM

Arequipa (1.2M people) depends on seven reservoirs fed by the Chili river headwaters. 2023: storage fell to 159/409 hm³, 70 districts in emergency. 2025: floods pushed turbidity to 5,000 NTU and 70%+ of the city lost tap water. Aguada Blanca reservoir lost half its capacity (43 → ~22 hm³) to sediment. Officials publicly disagreed on whether there was even a shortage. Ground stations cannot settle it. Satellites can, if you know which variables to look at and which trends to believe. That is exactly this challenge.

WHAT IT DOES

TerraVerdict is a geospatial data-science system of six chained modules:

• M0 Traceable ingestion: NASA POWER, GPM IMERG Final daily 1998–2025, MODIS LST, GIBS, Global Landslide Catalog, plus NOAA, USGS, CHIRPS, Copernicus. 142 raw files, each with a SHA-256 hash; one command verifies nothing was altered.

• M1 Relevance Matrix: which variables truly drive extreme rain? Two models, block permutation importance, 200-resample stability, FDR-controlled significance, single final test on 2021–2025.

• M2 Trend Detective + Confidence Seal: Sen slope, Mann-Kendall, ENSO removal, every ≥20-year window, independent data families and "years needed to decide". Finding: the headwaters warm +0.23 °C/decade (90% CI 0.15–0.30, p<0.001, 100% of windows agree), but rainfall has NO decidable trend. Anyone claiming "it rains less" has no support.

• M4 Anticipation: 10 neural networks (LSTM, GRU, iTransformer, DLinear, ...) vs classical models and ensembles. Frozen split (train 1981–2015, validation 2016–2020, test 2021–2026), test used once. All 7 published forecasts have CONFIRMED skill (90% CI > 0 AND Diebold-Mariano p<0.10): drought SPI-3 1-month skill 0.68, extreme rain next-day 0.09. Conformal 90% prediction cones, abstention when unsure, 2016–2026 out-of-sample track record. Models without skill are never shown.

• National scale: Confidence Seal, SPI drought and seismicity for all 25 regions of Peru; five hazards (extreme rain, drought, earthquakes, volcanoes, landslides).

• M6 Interface: bilingual (EN/ES) React app with a satellite map, ENSO simulator, master table, scientific charts, REST API (FastAPI, /api/docs) and "Terra", an AI assistant (Google Gemini) that answers ONLY from published evidence files, cites them, and passes every number through a deterministic verifier.

WHY IT MATTERS

A strong El Niño is under way right now (ONI ASO 2026 = +2.46). Our data show strong El Niño seasons average 98 mm of Dec–Mar rain vs 171 mm in La Niña years (r = −0.345, p = 0.024), but not always: 1983 had 5 mm, 2024 had 201 mm. So the city needs probabilistic, honest forecasts, not slogans. TerraVerdict tells water managers what to believe, what not to believe yet, and where to invest the conservation fund. The method works for any mountain basin on Earth.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

It is built to refuse overclaiming: every number on screen traces back to a reproducible evidence file (data hash + code commit + pre-registration). We audited our own metrics (19 findings fixed), verified 40 data sources against official catalogs, and separate clearly what is done from what is promised.

TOOLS

Python 3.12, PyTorch, scikit-learn, NumPy, FastAPI, React, Google Gemini, Playwright (end-to-end tests), GitHub Actions CI, Docker, Vercel.

Live app: https://terraverdict.vercel.app

Code: https://github.com/OwerLopez/terraverdict

Experimental results: not official alerts (SENAMHI, IGP, INGEMMET, INDECI).
